content: 1. Active oversight and management must be ensured, along with the fulfillment and coordination of Public-Private Mix (PPM) roles and responsibilities among the National Tuberculosis Program (NTP) and its partners. 2. By the end of 2016, the effective functioning of the PPM Committee and Technical Working Group (TWG) in representing and implementing PPM should be established. 3. Once strategic objectives, sub-objectives, activities, and targets have been decided, the group should develop a costed version of the national action plan for PPM. The WHO planning and budgeting tool may be utilized to support this process. 4. Activities should be grouped by lead organization, and each organization should be tasked with costing out their respective activities or packages of activities. Organizations may expand each activity into detailed budget lines for more robust costing, using standard cost categories. 5. For each PPM model represented in the strategic objectives, the lead organization should calculate the costs of expansion to meet the targets. This process can be standardized using cost categories, and funding gaps should be noted by marking n/a in the final column. 6. If human resource (HR) requirements are complex, existing positions, their numbers, rank, location, salary, and funding sources should be documented. The number of new staff needed should then be calculated and summarized. 7. A consultant should consolidate all information into a single master Excel sheet. The first tab should present a master budget, while individual contributions from partners can be included as backup tabs. 8. Costing should account for inflation, salary increases, and target expansion over time. Participants should review the cost per case for each model and compare costs between Year 1 and Year 5 to assess efficiency and program reach. 9. Once consultations are completed and stakeholders agree on task mixes, targets, strategic objectives, sub-objectives, activities, costing, and cost per case, the written report should be finalized. The report should include sections such as introduction, objectives, process considerations, situation analysis, goals, task mix, targets, sub-objectives, activities, and costing. 10. The finalized PPM national action plan should be adopted with high-level clearance from NTP leadership, the Director of Disease Control, and, if possible, the Health Secretary or Minister of Health. 11. The strategies and financial tables from the PPM national action plan should be incorporated into the country’s TB national strategic plan, Global Fund concept notes, donor proposals, and national budgeting processes. 12. A draft agenda for national consultations should be prepared, including steps to introduce PPM action planning, review the current PPM situation, develop strategic goals, prioritize models, identify providers and support systems, and map HR and cost requirements. 13. The expected outcome of the workshop is a first draft of the plan ready for dissemination to key stakeholders for feedback. Workshop methodologies should include PowerPoint presentations, group work, and group presentations.
